text:
maya_support: FYI customer (AcmeOps) reporting a burst of 504s and 502s on /v1/rerank yesterday afternoon at ~3pm UTC. p95 shot from 120ms -> 2.3s. Request IDs: abc123, def456. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.example/err-acme-3pm.png
liam_runtime: :eyes: do we have traces for abc123? rough QPS and batch sizes?
maya_support: They said they send batches of 500 candidates (list length varies 200-500), single request per user flow, QPS ~40 sustained for a 10m window, peak 120 qps for ~30s. Using model: rerank-7b-v2. Headers from a failing request: `X-Request-ID: abc123`, `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>`.
liam_runtime: That batch size is huge for rerank in our current config. Gateway has a default per-request token limit and backend concurrency that can cause queueing. Can you paste an example payload (trimmed) and any gateway logs?
maya_support: Pasted sample payload (trimmed):
```json
{"query":"best laptop","candidates":["item1","item2",..."item500"]}
```
And gateway log snippet:
```
2026-03-10T15:02:12Z gateway ERROR request=abc123 upstream_timeout=1.5s backend_retries=2 status=504
2026-03-10T15:02:12Z worker  WARN request=abc123 queue_wait=0.9s kv_cache_miss=1
```
sophie_sre: I'm seeing NLB 502 spikes aligned to that window, plus a surge in connection resets from the worker fleet. Might be worker queue pressure / OOM/GPU memory churn.
liam_runtime: Could be two things: (1) massive candidate lists cause per-request compute to spike (and block the worker thread) and (2) gateway retry loop is compounding the pressure (retries -> more load). Can we confirm backend did the full token computation each time vs hitting prefix cache?
maya_support: Customer says they do not set cache keys; looks like KV cache hit rate was very low for that workload.
jon_sales: AcmeOps is on Dedicated trial but currently routed through hosted gateway. Can we propose a mitigation we can tell them now? They are very sensitive to SLAs.
sophie_sre: Immediate mitigations: (a) throttle batch_size at gateway (reject >128 candidates with 429 + helpful message), (b) reduce max backend retries from 3->1 for rerank route, (c) temporarily enable autoscale aggressive policy for rerank-7b-v2. I'll queue change (impact assessment: low).
liam_runtime: Also suggest a fast fallback path: if candidate_count > 128, route to rerank-7b-quantized (lower memory/time but slightly lower quality) or do chunked rerank (split into 128 windows and do partial scores). We should add a short-term feature flag.
maya_support: Customer ok with being throttled, prefer chunking with progress indicator rather than 429. They asked for repro steps so they can validate.
liam_runtime: Repro steps for eng to reproduce locally:
1) curl to /v1/rerank with batch of 400 candidates (see payload)
2) set QPS=80 sustained for 2 minutes (wrk or k6 script)
3) use model rerank-7b-v2 with default concurrency
Sample wrk command:```bash
wrk -t4 -c60 -d120s -s rerank-script.lua -- 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank'
```
rerank-script.lua should POST the sample payload with Authorization header and rotate queries.
liam_runtime: Add debug flags on gateway to not retry on 5xx for this route and enable trace sampling 100% for the test.
sophie_sre: I'm running a short repro on staging now, spinning up 50 workers. If I can reproduce, I'll capture pprof/heap profiles and publish.
maya_support: Customer asked if tokenization could be the bottleneck (they send long text in candidates). Any quick checks?
liam_runtime: Tokenization cost scales with candidate length. Two quick checks: 1) sample token count for those 500 candidates (avg token_len) and 2) run local single-request timing with model lib to measure per-candidate latency. If avg token_len > 200 then big factor.
jon_sales: Also flag billing: customer saw a sudden bill jump during that window — likely due to retries inflating token counts. Please include rough cost delta if we can.
sophie_sre: Staging repro: initial run shows worker queue_wait p95=1.1s at QPS=80 with 400 candidates. Enabling retries_off reduced gateway p95 but backend still saturates. Heap trace points to kv-cache thrash and big transient allocations.
liam_runtime: Action items:
- sophie_sre: finish heap/pprof and upload to incident doc (owner)
- liam_runtime: push quick flag: route >128->chunked fallback to rerank-7b-quant (owner)
- maya_support: communicate temporary guidance to AcmeOps (limit candidate_size to 128 or enable chunking)
- jon_sales: notify customer success about billing/credits conversation
I'm assigning owners in the thread. ETA for mitigation rollout: 2 hours for feature-flag path, 30m for throttling rule.
maya_support: Thanks, please keep me posted. I'll post customer confirmation when they validate. :thumbsup: 
deploy-bot: deploy started for service=routing-config by liam_runtime at 2026-03-10T17:05:00Z
sophie_sre: deploy succeeded, routing-config updated: rerank route max_candidates=128, backend_retries=1, fallback_model=rerank-7b-quant. Monitoring link: https://monitor.redwood.example/d/abc/rerank-load
maya_support: Customer validated on their side with chunked requests, p95 back to ~140ms, they reported no 5xx after change. Closing for now unless we see recurrence.
liam_runtime: Follow ups: longer-term we should add an automatic detection and per-client rate limit policy, and tune KV cache eviction for heavy candidate workflows. I'll open a GH ticket.
maya_support: Filed support ticket SUM-5621 for follow-up work and cost reconciliation.
sophie_sre: Marking this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
